Art and Architecture Under Delhi Sultanate
The new features broughtby the Turkish conquerors were : (i) the dome
(i) the lofty towers (iii) the true arch unsupported by beam (v)the
vault:
They also broughtwith them an expert knowledge ofthe use of concrete
and mortar; which had hitherto been little used in India
The Adhai-din ka Jhonpra at Ajmer has beautiful prayer hall, an
exquisitely carved Mehrab of white marble and decorative arch
screen.
The first example of true or voussoired arch is said to be the tomb of
Ghiyasuddin Balbanin Mehrauli (Delhi)
In the Khilji period the usage of voussoired arch and dome was
established and for all. Famous examples is the tomb of Hazrat
Nizamuddin Aulia at Delhi-
The Tughlaq buildings show stark simplicity and sobriety probably
indicating less financial resources as well as puritanical testsSlopping
walls and dark appearance characterise the buildings. Some notable
Tughlaq monuments were the fort of Tughlaquabad, the tomb of
Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq which marked new phase in Indo-Islamic
architecture by serving Adilabad as model for later tombs and the fort of
The Sayyid period was too short to allow construction of elaborate
buildings.
